summary: This article explains how matter exists as solids, liquids and gases, why tiny particles make each state behave differently, and how heating and cooling change one state into another.
introduce: Write “Alike” and “Different” at the top of a T-chart on the board and ask students to compare two school subjects in one minute. Explain that “Solids, Liquids and Gases” asks them to make the same kind of comparison.

keyTerms.def: a very tiny piece of something
to shake quickly back and forth in a small space
something that holds things inside it, like a box, jar, or bottle

challengeTerms.def: the amount of space that something takes up
to become larger or spread out to take up more space
the process of removing salt from seawater to make fresh water

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that heating and cooling are the most important ways to change matter? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain what happens to the particles of water as ice melts and then boils.
struggling: Pre-teach particle, vibrate, and container with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers fill in a T-chart of alike and different with sentence starters.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses volume, expand, and desalination to compare two ideas from the article and explain which difference matters most.
